claims.text: Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems can be used for a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Conventional alloys constitute the initial or comparison material.
The proposed intervention is replacing conventional alloys with compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems.
The relevant behavior occurs within a narrow temperature window.
Alloy composition is the structural mediator of the proposed behavior.
Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys provide resistance to temper embrittlement.
The predicted outcome is a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Conventional alloys exhibiting temper embrittlement provide the baseline.
Temperature range bounds the proposed effect.
Observation of temper embrittlement in a compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy within a narrow temperature window would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Temper-embrittlement resistance is presented as the mechanism, but the predicted outcome includes an intervening brittle regime. No explanation is given for how resistance to embrittlement produces rather than suppresses that regime.

The hypothesis predicts ductile–brittle–ductile behavior, while the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis if the proposed alloys exhibit temper embrittlement within a narrow temperature window. Because the brittle interval is not operationally distinguished from temper embrittlement, the predicted observation could also be classified as falsifying.
